title: Interconnect bottleneck fingerprinting: long-context latency investigation
content:
Summary:

This is a working note capturing an experimental run and early analysis for isolating interconnect-induced latency spikes when serving long-context workloads across A100, H100 and L40S SKUs in multiple cloud regions. The emphasis here is on fingerprinting NVLink vs PCIe path behavior under decode-heavy and prefill-heavy traffic patterns, cross-checking driver and CUDA variants, and decomposing jitter into host, DMA, kernel, and NVLink/PCIe phases. The goal is to produce repeatable microbenchmarks we can add to perf dashboards and a set of mitigations/heuristics for routing and fallback at request time.

Motivation / Background:

- Customers see intermittent p99 regressions on long-context summarization and few-shot prompts; trends correlate with specific regions and occasional driver rollouts.
- Existing benches mostly measure throughput or sustained latency; we need phase-level attribution (host copy stalls vs kernel decode stalls vs interconnect stalls) for decoding pipelines that use large KV caches and long token windows (>8k).
- Prior experiments (see linked artifacts) explored clock/voltage and firmware; this work focuses on interconnect fingerprinting and how different cloud SKUs expose pathologies.

Testbed and methodology (high level):

- SKUs: NVIDIA A100 80GB, H100 80GB, L40S (80GB equivalent) instances across 3 clouds (aws-us-west-2, gcp-europe-west1, azure-eastus2). Instance families chosen to represent common customers.
- Driver/CUDA variants: Nvidia driver 535.X with CUDA 12.2, driver 525.X with CUDA 11.8, and a Samsung-edge older 470/11.4-style pairing where available. We deliberately included two widely deployed driver stacks + one older variant to surface epochal differences.
- Workloads: two synthetic traces derived from production logs:
  1) long-prefill (avg prompt 2k tokens, prefill-heavy: 90% tokens in first pass, large KV writes)
  2) rolling-decode (sliding window of 8k context with steady decode, frequent KV hits)
- Sampling and tools: eBPF user-space probes to tag host->device memcpy enter/exit, nv-host-client traces for nvlink stats, kernel launch counters from CUPTI, and our runtime-level per-token breakdown hooks (host-copy, enqueue, kernel, postcopy). We also collected perf counters for PCIe DMA stalls where supported.
- Runs: repeated 20 runs per SKU/CUDA/driver/trace, at low (1 concurrent session), medium (8 sessions), and burst (32 sessions) concurrency. Each run recorded p50/p95/p99, jitter distribution, kernel launch rate, host-copy stall durations, and NVLink error counters.

Configuration matrix (short):

- SKUs x driver/cuda x concurrency x trace type = ~540 experimental cells. We prioritized cells that map to current production fleets (aws and gcp first).

Key observations (raw-ish):

- H100 (cuda12.2/driver535) under rolling-decode shows the best median decode throughput but exhibits rare p99 spikes that align tightly with elevated host->device memcpy durations (host stalls). p50/p95/p99 (rolling-decode, single session): H100: 18ms / 28ms / 95ms (note: median is for decode path only).
- A100 (cuda11.8/driver525) shows slightly higher medians but much smoother tails: 24ms / 34ms / 48ms. NVLink counters show fewer DMA retry events in our sample runs compared to H100 runs with identical workloads.
- L40S (cuda12.2) medians comparable to A100 in our config but with occasional 200-400ms excursions during high concurrency burst tests. Those align with PCIe link retraining events visible in host syslogs (rare but catastrophic for in-flight KV cache repopulation).
- Driver mismatch cases (older driver on newer hw) produce systematic small increases in kernel launch latency and a wider distribution of host-copy durations, presumably due to suboptimal kernel scheduling or DMA path fallback.

Phase attribution patterns (decomposition):

- For H100 p99 spikes, timeline decomposition shows: rapid sequence of kernel launches (decode), then abrupt host-copy stall of 30–150ms, followed by a backlog of enqueued kernels. eBPF captures show the host-side memcpy entering a wait state while DMA engine is idle (suggests device-side backpressure or transient interconnect error).
- A100 p99 events are mostly kernel-latency dominated (single noisy kernel), not host-copy stalls.
- L40S p99 events often correlate with host GPU isolation events (PCIe link state transitions reported by kernel), frequently during node-level network activity or noisy neighbor bursts.

Hypotheses (ranked):

1) NVLink buffer exhaustion/backpressure on H100 under rolling-decode + KV cache churn leads to transient DMA scheduling stalls on the host, manifesting as host-copy wait states while device still accepts kernels.
2) A100 microarchitectural differences make kernel-level slowdowns more likely than interconnect stalls, so mitigation focuses on kernel pacing and preemption-aware scheduling.
3) L40S firmware/slot-level PCIe retraining is more likely in certain cloud rack configs; noisy neighbor IO triggers retrain and long tail.
4) Driver/CUDA mismatches degrade DMA paths and kernel launch fast-paths, widening jitter distributions.

Evidence and cross-checks: 

- We correlated p99 events with nvlink error counters and host PCIe retrain entries in syslog; H100 p99 events had elevated NVLINK_RETRY counters in 7/10 samples, L40S p99 events correlated with PCIe AER messages in 5/6 cases.
- Re-running H100 rolling-decode with KV write batching (reduce frequency of large host->device transfers) reduced p99 from ~95ms to ~36ms in isolated runs — strong evidence for interconnect/backpressure.
- Running A100 with patched CUDA kernel shuffle (experimental PR) reduced kernel tail but did not affect host-copy durations.

Immediate mitigations to trial in staging:

- Dynamic prefill batching: combine small KV writes into fewer host->device transfers to reduce NVLink DMA churn. Deploy as an optional runtime knob.
- Soft rate-limiter on enqueue: when host-copy stall metric climbs beyond threshold, throttle new prefill writes to allow DMA backlog drain.
- Driver compatibility gating: enforce known-good driver/CUDA pairs for production fleets; flag rollouts that deviate and force canary via routing policy.
- Cloud-routing heuristic: prefer A100 for highest-sustained long-context throughput when kernel-dominant tails are acceptable; prefer H100 only when median matters and interconnect appears healthy.

Open questions / follow-ups:

- Need larger sample across more racks and AZs to rule out provider-side cabling/topology issues. Current sample is biased to two racks per region.
- Can we instrument device-side DMA queues more precisely (NVIDIA telemetry hooks) to see device backpressure states? Follow PR to expand CUPTI metrics.
- Are there kernel-level scheduling knobs we can expose to reduce single-kernel noise on A100 (CUDA launch flags, realtime CPU affinity)?

Suggested next experiments (priority):

1) Controlled NVLink stress test: microbench that issues many small host->device memcpys while keeping kernel launch rate constant; measure DMA retry counters and host-copy wait times. Run on H100 & A100 across driver variants.
2) Rack-level sweep: repeat failing L40S workloads across more nodes in same AZ to see correlation with NIC and PCIe error logs (isolate noisy neighbors).
3) Canary rollout of prefill-batching in staging for rolling-decode workload with A/B routing and p99 monitoring.

Action items / owners:

- Implement prefill-batching prototype (Maya) — due 2025-06-23.
- Build NVLink microbench harness and add to perf CI (James) — due 2025-07-07.
- Expand telemetry to capture device DMA queue depth via CUPTI if possible (Lena) — investigate by 2025-06-30.

Notes to self / rough checklist:

- Keep raw trace logs from 2025-06-10 H100 runs (s3://infra-perf/interop/h100-longcontext-20250610/) — include in replication package.
- Add a short writeup for infra-runbook: what to do if p99 spikes show NVLink retry counters > threshold (call it nvlink-backpressure-runbook).

Appendix: quick table (representative single-session rolling-decode numbers):

- H100 (cuda12.2/535): p50 18ms | p95 28ms | p99 95ms | common phase: host-copy stall during spike
- A100 (cuda11.8/525): p50 24ms | p95 34ms | p99 48ms | common phase: noisy kernel
- L40S (cuda12.2): p50 26ms | p95 45ms | p99 210ms | common phase: PCIe retrain/host isolation

This is a working doc — expect edits, additional plots and raw histograms to be attached as separate files. The goal is to converge on a minimal set of runtime changes that reduce p99 for long-context traces across the fleet while providing clear canary checks when deploying new drivers or moving workloads between SKUs.
